Q: What exactly is a context of an expression? A:

Based on reading the "Place expressions and value expressions" section and its subsections, it seems like the main distinction is between "place context" and "value context". In a place context, the memory address that the expression refers to is determined, but the value at that location is not fetched. In contrast, in a value context, the final value is determined.

Q: Multi-tenant Azure apps - SPA & API - admin consent working A:

Root cause

The error:

AADSTS650052: The app is trying to access a service that your organization
lacks a service principal for

means the API application does not yet exist as a service principal in Tenant B.

This is expected behavior and indicates a misunderstanding of how admin consent works in multi-tenant scenarios, especially when SPA + API are involved.

Key misunderstanding

Admin consent does NOT automatically provision service principals for both the SPA and the API.

Only the application being consented gets a service principal created in the target tenant.

In your flow, you are running:

/organizations/v2.0/adminconsent

for the SPA application, but the SPA is requesting scopes from an API that does not yet exist in Tenant B.

Azure AD cannot grant consent for an API whose service principal has not been created yet, so the flow fails before showing any consent dialog.

Why no consent dialog appears

Consent dialogs are shown only after Azure AD can resolve all resource applications involved.

In your case:

  • SPA exists in Tenant A ✔

  • API exists in Tenant A ✔

  • SPA service principal exists in Tenant B ❌

  • API service principal exists in Tenant B ❌

Because the API service principal does not exist in Tenant B, Azure AD throws invalid_client instead of showing a consent UI.

Correct multi-tenant consent flow (important)

Step 1 — Admin consent the API application first

You must explicitly create the API service principal in Tenant B.

Run admin consent against the API app, not the SPA:

https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/adminconsent
  ?client_id=<API_CLIENT_ID>
  &redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>

✔ This creates the API service principal in Tenant B
✔ Grants admin-consented permissions (scopes / app roles)

Step 2 — Admin consent the SPA application

Once the API exists in Tenant B, you can then run admin consent for the SPA:

https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations/v2.0/adminconsent
  ?client_id=<SPA_CLIENT_ID>
  &redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>

Now Azure AD can:

  • Resolve the API resource

  • Show the consent dialog

  • Create the SPA service principal

  • Grant delegated permissions

Why organizations is correct (and not your problem)

Using:

/organizations

is correct when:

  • You don’t know the tenant ID in advance

  • You want any Azure AD tenant to onboard

The issue is not the endpoint — it’s the order of consent.

Why knownClientApplications did nothing

knownClientApplications is only used for:

  • Token issuance optimization

  • OBO / first-party scenarios

It does not create service principals
It does not affect consent flows

So adding IDs there has no effect in this case.

Why Microsoft docs mention authorize + prompt=admin_consent

That approach works because:

  • It implicitly forces the API resource to be resolved

  • It creates the service principal as a side effect

However, it hides the real issue and makes the flow harder to reason about.

Your instinct to understand why instead of applying it blindly is correct.

Summary

  • Admin consent is per application

  • API and SPA must be consented separately

  • The API must be consented first

  • Service principals are not auto-created transitively

  • Your configuration is mostly correct; the issue is flow order

Final takeaway

This is not a security block, tenant restriction, or misconfiguration.
It is simply how Azure AD models multi-tenant consent and service principal provisioning.

Q: Taking a server id, and resulting all channel id's in discord using python A:

The bot itself doesn't have access to the server, so it does not have access to the server channel ids. Therefore, Discord return 401 Unauthorized.

You have two options to solve this:

Option 1: Add the bot to the server

Option 2 (If you really don't want to add the bot): use your own Discord Authorization Token. You can find this by going into the browser version of Discord, opening the developer console, and going to the network tab. There, you can just click on any request (counts for example), go down to the "Request Headers" section, and copy and paste the "Authorization" header. This method is a bit more dangerous because you DO NOT WANT TO LEAK THIS!! If you leak this people will be able to access and do stuff to your account.

Q: What is the Windows equivalent for en_US.UTF-8 locale? A:

As of 2026, Windows supports the locale name "en_US.UTF-8", along with many variations. The canonical name returned by setlocale(LC_ALL, NULL) is "English_United States.utf8".

Q: how to automatically install Visual C++ Redistributable for Visual Studio 2015 used in a java code A:

If you already have bat file for install best way to do this will be to include install of vc_redist in this *.bat before install. From what I know it is not posiible to include this in the *.jar. Better will be to pack all files into zip (together with this *.bat script).

To install vcredist in bat silently you will have to add these commands:

@echo OFF
reg Query "HKLM\Hardware\Description\System\CentralProcessor\0" | find /i "x86" > NUL && set OS=32BIT || set OS=64BIT

if %OS%==32BIT runas /user:Administrator %~dp0\vcredist_x86.exe /q /norestart
if %OS%==64BIT runas /user:Administrator %~dp0\vcredist_x64.exe /q /norestart

#rest of your script

Checking if system is 32bit of 64bit is taken from here (batch file to check 64bit or 32bit OS)

%~dp0 resolves to the full path of the folder in which the batch script resides.

Edit:

As the runas might not be the best solution to problem of running this as administrator I will direct you to these posts to read about running with administrator privilages in bat

How to code a BAT file to always run as admin mode?

How can I auto-elevate my batch file, so that it requests from UAC administrator rights if required?

Q: Strange "pattern not match" error on fluentd A:

The problem is that these ELB-HealthChecker line log has an empty referer ip field. And then the log doesn't match apache2 log format for fluentd.

So the way to fix that is to filter logs with ELB-HealthChecker user-agent.

Q: gitolite gitlist: Failed to resolve HEAD as a valid ref A:

I suffered from this problem, too.

In a bare repository "repoName.git" there is probably this file: -rw-r--r-- 1 git git 23 Sep 19 11:37 HEAD with the content: ref: refs/heads/master. Similar postings suggested to check the access rights for this file.

But when I examined the file repoName.git/refs/heads/master it had these rights -rw------- 1 git git 41 Mar 13 15:22 refs/heads/master.

Therefore I could solve this problem by changing the rights for this file too (actually I granted a little more, you can try to give less rights):

chmod go+r repositories

Where 'repositories' is the repositories directory of gitolite.

Q: What is the purpose of PyPy if one cannot use the latest Python features? A:

Different people/organizations and projects may have different priorities in terms of performance, features, and security.

For example, for computing some kind of simulation, speed may be critical, whereas security may be irrelevant if all the input data is trustworthy, and the older features may be enough.
